dataset.name: GB1 four-site landscape, Wu et al. 2016 Supplementary file 1

paper.title: Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths

raw_files.role: official Supplementary file 1, measured/profiled variant fitness table
RCSB PDB structure file; chain A records reference domain sequence
RCSB PDB official FASTA structural reference sequence for chain A; not the assay template
official Figure 1 supplement 1 image showing structural mapping and WT nucleotide-template translation

excluded_imputed_file.role: official Supplementary file 2, imputed fitness values for missing variants

assay.target: GB1 domain B1 binding to IgG-Fc, measured using mRNA display and sequencing selection
assay.fitness_definition: Fitness is relative to wild type (WT), for which Fitness=1; the paper derives scores from relative sequence frequencies before and after selection.
assay.direction: Higher Fitness is better within this assay.
assay.imputation_policy: Use Supplementary file 1 only for experiment-derived training/oracle values. Supplementary file 2 is explicitly imputed and was not downloaded or merged.
assay.single_mutation_calibration: The paper states that single-substitution fitness values were taken from Olson et al. 2014 due to higher sequencing coverage there and multiplied by 1.159, based on a linear fit with approximately zero intercept. These are experiment-based, cross-study-calibrated values, not a fresh remeasurement of each single mutant in Wu et al. 2016.

single_mutation_source.title: A comprehensive biophysical description of pairwise epistasis throughout an entire protein domain

workbook_audit.audit_status: All rows have a unique, valid four-residue variant, complete values in all five columns, and HD equal to the Hamming distance from VDGV.

reference_sequence.sequence_role: Wu et al. 2016 assay WT GB1 B1-domain coding template, translated from Figure 1 supplement 1 panel B
reference_sequence.sequence_source: The figure caption identifies this as the WT nucleotide template and attributes it to Olson et al. 2014.

olson_2014_source.title: A comprehensive biophysical description of pairwise epistasis throughout an entire protein domain

n_terminal_translation_check.upstream_sequence: Figure shows a T7 promoter and 5-prime untranslated template sequence before the GB1 start codon ATG.
n_terminal_translation_check.indexing_conclusion: The first translated Met is GB1-domain position 1; no extra amino-acid offset is applied.

reference_sequence.mapping_note: Use 1-based local positions in the 56-aa experimental GB1-domain template above. The S1 Variants field stores only the four amino acids in the order 39, 40, 41, 54. Reconstruct full-domain candidates from this MQY... template, replacing those four positions. The experimental template's residue 2 is Gln (Q), not Thr (T).

structural_reference.pdb_title: Two crystal structures of the B1 immunoglobulin-binding domain of streptococcal protein G and comparison with NMR
structural_reference.citation: Gallagher T, Alexander P, Bryan P, Gilliland GL. Biochemistry. 1994;33:4721-4729. DOI: 10.1021/bi00181a032.
structural_reference.sequence_source_verification: The sequence parsed from chain A SEQRES records in the downloaded 1PGA.pdb exactly matches the downloaded 1PGA.fasta sequence.
structural_reference.role: Structural position reference only. Wu et al. Figure 1 supplement 1 panel A uses 1PGA to locate the mutated sites. Its chain-A sequence has Thr at position 2, whereas the assay construct shown in panel B has Gln at position 2.

processing_notes.structural_sequence_validation_method: Parse SEQRES records for chain A in 1PGA.pdb and compare to downloaded 1PGA.fasta; no sequence mismatch.
processing_notes.experimental_template_validation_method: Read the official eLife Figure 1 supplement 1 panel B image. Its caption identifies the displayed WT nucleotide template as Olson et al. 2014; the displayed translated sequence starts Met-Gln and the first two shown codons are ATG-CAG. The full displayed 56-aa translation is recorded separately under reference_sequence.
